comment: brief TRN-7 R-trn7-2. micromamba's single static program, checksummed, installs conda-forge's ngspice into an environment of circuitRF's own: no conda installation of the user's is read or changed. conda-forge's newest ngspice is 41, and it builds none for arm64 (checked 2026-11-15 on its package index), so macOS arm64 and Linux arm64 have no recipe and say so instead. The same steps as the Linux x64 recipe, which was run end to end in a container; this one has not been run on an Intel Mac.
layoutNote: A conda environment writes its own absolute path into the files it installs, so the home is built where it stays.

sources.checksumNote: micromamba 2.10.0 checks every package it downloads against the SHA-256 conda-forge's index lists for it; ngspice-exe is pinned to its exact build, 41 h6811dc0_0

consentNotes: ngspice is free software under the modified BSD licence, with parts under other free licences listed in its own documentation; circuitRF starts it as a separate program and distributes nothing.
micromamba is free software under the BSD licence; circuitRF runs it only to install ngspice and deletes it afterwards.

steps.name: Install ngspice 41 from conda-forge
steps.comment: --no-rc and --override-channels: no .condarc of the user's, and no channel but conda-forge, plays any part.

steps.name: Clear micromamba's package cache
steps.comment: The cache holds every package a second time, and nothing reads it again. clean takes no --root-prefix: it reads MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX, which this recipe sets.

measured.source: not run on an Intel Mac; the same steps on Linux x64 took 25 s and 0.17 GB
